PullRequest.Title: Fix Quick Pick item tooltip clipping and relayout (#174900)
PullRequest.Body:
🤖 This PR was prepared by an AI agent (GitHub Copilot) for review by @sbatten.

Fixes #174900

## Problem

Quick Pick item tooltips (`IQuickPickItem.tooltip`) were laid out badly, and it is broader than images:

- **Modern UI (default).** The tooltip's context view was `position: absolute` inside `.quick-input-widget`, which has `overflow: hidden`. The tooltip was clipped and only the pointer sliver showed. When Tab focused a link inside it, the widget's hidden overflow scrolled and pushed the input and rows out of view.
- **Modern UI off.** The widget is still the containing block, so a side tooltip shrink-wrapped to a ~79 px column pinned to the top, with its pointer detached from the row. In a short window, keyboard invocation showed nothing.
- **Delayed content (images).** `HoverWidget` kept its last fallback side, so the hover never returned to the requested side. It compared the unclamped height against the window for the vertical fallback, and it kept inline pointer offsets from the previous axis. After an image loaded, the pointer ended up inside the hover.

## Changes

- `QuickInputList` owns a viewport-sized host (`.quick-input-list-hover-host`: `position: fixed; inset: 0; pointer-events: none`, with `pointer-events: auto` on its `.context-view` child) inside the list, and passes it as the item hover's `container`. The hover service keeps its normal absolute context view, so **the hover API and `HoverService` are unchanged from `main`**. The hover stays a DOM descendant of the widget, so the focus tracker and Tab into the tooltip behave as before, while the widget's `overflow: hidden` and size no longer affect it. (An earlier revision of this PR added a public `useFixedPosition` hover option instead; it was replaced to keep this Quick Input-specific concern out of the hover API.)
- `QuickInputController` *settles* the entrance animation, so the widget stops being a containing block for the fixed-position host (`animation: none; will-change: auto` via `quick-input-widget-motion-settled`).
  - It settles when `quick-input-widget-open` ends, or right before an item tooltip is measured.
  - The marker is removed only on a hidden → visible `show()`. Tooltip toggles and visible controller replacement don't replay the animation, and the close animation is kept (`:not(.quick-input-widget-closing)`).
- `HoverWidget.layout()`:
  - re-starts from the requested position on every layout;
  - uses `min(height, maxHeight)` for the ABOVE/BELOW fallback;
  - clamps LEFT/RIGHT hovers vertically into the window (not when `forcePosition` is set);
  - clears stale inline pointer `top`/`left` before positioning;
  - only applies the LEFT branch's trailing bounds check while the hover is still LEFT, so a BELOW fallback for a LEFT-requested hover is no longer overwritten with RIGHT (pre-existing on `main`, made persistent by the per-layout reset; found by Copilot review).
- `QuickInputList` dismisses the item hover when the list has moved since it was shown (window resize, alignment change, re-centring), since a viewport-positioned hover no longer follows the picker; relayouts in place keep it (found by Copilot review).

No image-load callback is added: markdown hovers already re-layout when their content changes.

## Tests

The tests run under `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --run src/vs/platform/hover/test/browser/hoverService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/browser/quickinput.test.ts --browser chromium`:
- **With this change:** 111 passing.
- **Without the production changes:** the 7 new tests fail on behavioural assertions, not setup.
- **Without only the pointer-offset reset:** the fallback test fails on the stale pointer position.

New tests:

- `HoverService` (`showInstantHover`):
  - the fallback chain re-evaluates as content changes, including computed pointer placement;
  - the clamped vertical fallback;
  - a tall side hover stays in the window with the pointer on the target;
  - an ABOVE-requested hover re-evaluates ABOVE → BELOW → ABOVE (fails on `main`, where it stays BELOW);
  - a LEFT-requested hover re-evaluates LEFT → RIGHT → BELOW and back (fails on `main` and without the LEFT guard).
- `QuickInput item hover layout` uses a real controller, real `HoverService` and real CSS, with Modern UI + motion on and frosted glass off. It checks:
  - the item hover renders in an absolute context view that is a direct child of the viewport-sized host inside the list, and only the hover receives pointer events (fails on the previous `useFixedPosition` revision);
  - geometry during and after the open animation;
  - no animation replay when tooltips are hidden or replaced, fail to show, or lose their items;
  - a visible picker → picker → input box replacement keeps the widget settled, the close animation runs, and a new show animates;
  - the item hover is dismissed when the picker moves and kept when it is relaid out in place.

## Manual verification

Same base commit, unfixed vs fixed. A deterministic one-item Quick Pick with text tooltips, and an image tooltip whose request is held for 1.5 s:

- **macOS desktop (Code OSS dev):**
  - mouse and Ctrl+Space;
  - Modern UI on/off and frosted glass on/off;
  - windows of 1400×900, 1000×700, 760×520 and 700×500;
  - the picker dragged to the right edge, so only LEFT fits.

  The tooltip is visible in every sampled frame (vs 0 before in Modern UI), stays inside the window, and has 0 px pointer error. After the image loads it re-lays out exactly once, with no oscillation.
- **Keyboard:** Ctrl+Space → Tab → tooltip → link → Escape gives the same focus order and dismissal as before. The focused tooltip is now visible.
- **Web** (code-server + Chromium): same before/after result for the default-setting scenarios.
- **Not verified:** Windows/Linux desktop and high-contrast themes.

## Notes

- `HoverWidget` geometry changes affect all workbench hovers. They only matter when a hover re-lays out, overflows the window vertically, or changes axis.
- These open PRs touch nearby code and may need a trivial rebase:
  - #316992, the same reset block in `HoverWidget.layout()`;
  - #332608, Quick Input.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show and navigate a Quick Pick item tooltip
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The keyboard/mouse tooltip action calls QuickInputList.showHover, settles the entrance animation, lazily creates the fixed hover host, and synchronously renders and lays out one HoverWidget before it is visible. This work is on the tooltip-display critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tooltip focus changes while the Quick Pick is open. Only one item hover is live at a time; changing focus disposes the prior hover, and the host is created once per QuickInputList.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM construction and layout run serially on the UI thread; HoverService replacement prevents a burst of concurrent top-level item hovers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The viewport host is lazy on the first tooltip and reused thereafter. A hidden controller keeps only that single host under its hidden subtree; disposing the controller disposes/removes the parent subtree. Hover contents themselves are not newly cached by this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed showHover path, one-host lazy initialization, and prior-hover disposal are explicit in QuickInputList and HoverService.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact hover layout duration varies with tooltip markup and DOM size, but the diff adds only constant class/host work and does not increase active-hover cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new work is bounded to first use or one class update per hover, while existing HoverWidget rendering/layout remains the dominant synchronous work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize, realign, relayout, or drag a Quick Pick while an item tooltip is shown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: QuickInputController.updateLayout writes picker geometry, lays out the list/tree, then the new hideHoverIfMoved check reads the list rectangle and synchronously disposes the hover if its viewport position changed. The geometry read is on the relayout event's UI-thread critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Host resize/layout events, content-height updates, and drag updates while a tooltip is live. An actual position change disposes the tooltip on the first such event; unchanged-position relayouts can repeat one rectangle read per event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events are serialized on the UI thread. There is no queue, subprocess, IPC, or asynchronous fan-out; drag and resize updates invoke layout synchronously.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The recorded top/left pair is captured once when the hover is shown. Once the hover is disposed, the isDisposed guard skips subsequent geometry reads until another tooltip is shown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed read-after-write path and its one-movement bound; medium for any measurable browser cost because tree layout already performs substantial synchronous DOM work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A rectangle read can force style/layout after preceding writes, but the movement case is self-bounding after one event and unchanged-position events already execute list/tree layout; there is insufficient evidence of meaningful added frame cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The only plausible synchronous-layout cost is guarded by a live hover and ceases on the first movement, so the diff does not establish realistic repeated jank or scaling regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Relayout a workbench hover after delayed or dynamically resized content, including an image tooltip
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A markdown async-render callback or HTML ResizeObserver invokes HoverWidget.layout. The diff now restores the requested side, clears two pointer offsets, and clamps side-hover geometry during that existing synchronous measurement/layout pass before the context view is updated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The browser may fetch an image referenced by pre-existing markdown hover content; completion can trigger the existing async render/layout callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the markdown document's referenced image requests for the active hover, subject to browser URL caching; the diff does not add or duplicate requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same markdown rendering and image fetch occurred before the PR and already triggered hover relayout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The fetch is off the initial hover-display critical path; its completion causes a synchronous relayout of the already shown hover.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Content resize notifications for the single active hover (with bounded nested-hover depth). Cost grows with resize callback frequency, not Quick Pick item count; the changed operations are constant per callback.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hover layout callbacks execute serially on the UI thread. Image downloads are browser-scheduled; each completed content update triggers the existing layout callback path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm browser image-cache hits can avoid a delayed network completion; cold image loads retain existing browser caching behavior. The diff adds no application cache, retry loop, or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ResizeObserver/async-render call paths and the changed constant-time operations are explicit; no changed boundary cardinality or retained collection is present.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Dynamic content and callback counts vary, but the added state reset and style clears are constant and execute inside a path that already performs multiple geometry reads and writes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR changes placement decisions during an existing relayout without adding callbacks, network requests, collection-wide work, or unbounded retained state.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. Traced tooltip creation/navigation, quick-input movement/layout, animation settlement and host lifetime, and global dynamic hover relayout. No diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold; no findings or regression-fix records were submitted.
